guitar.notes: Confirmed — Billy Gibbons' 1959 Les Paul "Pearly Gates" is one of the most famous guitars in rock history.

tone.target: tight Texas boogie crunch with biting midrange
tone.profile: tight Texas boogie crunch with biting midrange
tone.summary: Gate -> Boost/OD 9 -> DST (RAT-style) -> AMP (UK 50) -> CAB/IR (UK Vintage 4x12) -> EQ (Guitar EQ 2) -> Delay -> Room

rig.name: ZZ Top - Gimme All Your Lovin' - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and sustain.
Add initial grit and tighten the attack for boogie feel.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD 9/Green OD to maintain maximum punchiness without coloring the tone too much.

blocks.purpose: Provide the biting midrange and tight crunch required for Texas boogie.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style captures the aggressive, mid-focused grit better than Muff or Distortion for this specific genre requirement.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/Plexi sound and punchy British tone.
blocks.gap: The UK 50 is ideal for high-gain, mid-focused rock tones associated with ZZ Top's era.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic Marshall-style cabinet voicing and punch.
Enhance the upper-mid bite and cut any excessive low end, keeping the tone tight.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 allows for more precise mid-range boosting than EQ 1, crucial for 'upper-mid bite'.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic depth and space without sounding overly ambient.
blocks.gap: A short, controlled delay adds dimension suitable for boogie rhythms.

blocks.purpose: Provide a natural, dry room ambience to ground the aggressive tone.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is preferred over Plate/Spring for its less artificial and more 'dry' feel.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and overall punch by swapping the default IR for a more aggressive, vintage 4x12 voicing.

proposals.reason: Enhance punch and bite needed for Texas boogie feel.
